layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of nitrogen, which is one of the most important elements in duplex stainless steels (SSs), was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigated for resistance to pitting corrosion and stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments. The increase in nitrogen content increases the resistance of the base metal, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results from the improvement in the resistance of the γ-phase, which has lower chromium and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum contents compared to α-phase. Nitrogen is an important element in sustaining the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of the heat affected zone (HAZ), which is heated to 1350 C or higher, because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen promotes the formation of γ-phase during the cooling process after welding and avoids the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: precipitation of chromium carbides or nitrides at grain boundaries. When the nitrogen content is less

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: than 0.08% in 22%Cr, 5.5%Ni, and 3%Mo base composition, the HAZ has little γ-phase to lead to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high susceptibility to intergranular corrosion and intergranular stress corrosion cracking (IGSCC) occurs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: even in a pure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environment containing no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Nitrogen has little effect on the precipitation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: behavior of the other phase in the base metal during aging heat treatment of around 700 C.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The recent search for new sources of hydrocarbons has led to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: production from more severe environments. Such wells are deep and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: often constructed at offshore sites. The environments usually contain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considerable amounts of carbon dioxide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hydrogen sulfide

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (HS), and concentrated brine. Oil and gas production from these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: wells expose construction materials, such as tubulars and line pipes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to very severe corrosive conditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Low alloy steels are not suitable because inhibited systems are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not desirable for offshore use or for the high temperature portion of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the well. The corrosion resistance of highly alloyed materials, for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, duplex stainless steels (SSs), high nickel SSs, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nickel-base alloys have been evaluated for the purpose of selecting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proper materials depending on the various well condition.1-6Among

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those highly alloyed materials, 22%Cr duplex SS line pipes have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: “Submitted for publication June 1986; revised July 1987.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: been widely used in the field that contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and chloride ions with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: small amounts of H₂S. Duplex SSs usually contain some amount of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen to improve the corrosion and mechanical properties welded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: joints. Corrosion behaviors such as pitting, intergranular corrosion,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and SCC of 22%Cr duplex SS have been investigated by many

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: researchers.7,8 The effect of nitrogen on corrosion behavior, how-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ever, has not been clarified yet.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, the effect of nitrogen content on the corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance of 22%Cr duplex SSs was investigated with respect to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: base metals, the low temperature HAZ, and the high temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HAZ, which is heated to 1350 C or higher.

layout_dets.text: Test Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The pitting potential was measured potentiodynamically in 5%

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: NaCl deaerated solution at 60 C at a sweep rate of 20 mV/min with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a potentiostat. The (reference) SCE and the platinum counter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: electrode were used in this study. The test specimen, a disk 15 mm

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in diameter and 2 mm in thickness, was polished with No. 600 emery

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paper, washed with water and alcohol, and then degreased with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acetone. The potential at which the anodic current density increases

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dramatically by the occurrence of pitting was adopted as the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: potential (Vc’).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: Test Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Duplex SSs have a characteristic morphological change in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phase structure of welded joint, as shown in Figure 4. In general,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: there exist two kinds of HAZs at the welded joint; that is, the low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature heat affected zone (HAZ) where the microstructure does

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not change and the high temperature HAZ, which is heated to 1350

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: C or higher, and different phase structure from the base metal. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: HAZs are defined as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and (B) respectively in this paper.

layout_dets.text: Discussion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been shown that nitrogen is beneficial in improving the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion resistance of the base metal. This beneficial effect of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen can be attributed to improving the pitting corrosion resistant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the austenite phase, as discussed below. Chromium and molyb-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: denum contents in the ferrite and austenite phases are almost

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constant independent of nitrogen content, as shown in Figure 21. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite phase has ~21%Cr-2.5%Mo, while the ferrite phase has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 23%Cr-3.5%Mo. Assuming that the pitting index equation is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3Mo + 16N (as proposed in Reference 9) and that the nitrogen exists

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only in the austenite phase of 60%, as shown in Figure 1, the nitrogen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content required to get the same pitting corrosion resistance in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite phase as that in the ferrite phase is ~0.18%. Therefore, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion is thought to initiate at the austenite phase below the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nítrogen content of 0.18% from this rough estimation. Figure 22

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shows the microscopic observation of pitting initiation of the 22%Cr

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duplex SS in NaCi solution. In the alloys with nitrogen contents of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion is observed to initiate in austenite phase.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: When the nitrogen content increases to 0.164%, it can be seen that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting occurs at random on the ferrite and austenite phases. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: estimation mentioned above almost agrees with the observation.

layout_dets.text: Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effects of nitrogen content of 22%Cr duplex SS on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of welds was investigated. The results obtained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The increase in nitrogen content increases the resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting corrosion and SCC of the base metal, which results from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improvement in the resistance of austenite phase by the dissolved

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen itself.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Nitrogen has little effect on the intergranular corrosion at the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: low temperature HAZ in the Huey test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. More than 0.12% nitrogen is required for the 22%Cr, 5.5%Ni,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3%Mo base alloys to maintain the corrosion resistance at high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature HAZ, which is heated to 1350 C or higher. When the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nitrogen content is less than 0.077%, the HAZ, which contains little

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite phase, has the high susceptibility to intergranular corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and IGSCC.

layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The influence of grain boundary microstructure on the susceptibility of thermally treated (TT) Inconel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Alloy 600 to intergranular attack (IGA) and stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in 30%NaOH +

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at 350 C was investigated. Both mill-annealed (MA) and laboratory solution-annealed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloys were aged at 700 C to establish the effect of initial processing on the material's response to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thermal treatment. Treatments of 1 h or more at 700 C greatly improved the SCC resistance of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution-annealed material but did not improve the performance of MA material containing a high density

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of intragranular carbides. The poor behavior of this material after thermal treatment was associated with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the formation of small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: carbides qrowing at a high angle to the boundaries and the development

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of these into cellular colonies. This is attributed to the use of a MA temperature that was too low to take

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into solution sufficient carbon for the development of semicontinuous grain boundary carbides during

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the subsequent TT process.

layout_dets.text: Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mill-annealed (MA) Inconel Alloy 600, an austenitic nickel-based

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alloy, has been widely used for the manufacture of pressurized water

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reactor (PWR) steam-generator tubing since 1967.1 However, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combination of intergranular attack (IGA) and stress corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cracking (SCC) has occurred at the outer surfaces of the tubes in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Submitted for publication October 1986; revised March 1987.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: some steam generators where caustic impurities from the secondary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: water have concentrated in crevices between the tubes and adjacent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tube sheets or support plates.²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In recent years, thermal treatment (TT) after final MA has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used to improve the resistance of Alloy 600 to SCC in caustic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: environments.1 This treatment, at ~700 C for ~15 to 20 h, causes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chromium carbides to precipitate at the grain boundaries and allows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rehomogenization of the chromium content in the vicinity of most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundaries. It also reduces residual stresses and the effects of cold

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work introduced during the tubing manufacture. TT has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reported³ to significantly improve resistance to SCC for Alloy 600 with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: carbon contents in the range of 0.006 to 0.046% by weight. The
